prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1312; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Reported a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The claimant is driving, and the vehicle's rear quarter panel and passenger door show contact damage. The claimant reports a knee injury from striking the dashboard and has no attorney.

Entry 2: Police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene and that the other driver admitted to drifting into the lane. Two independent witnesses gave statements that match the claimant's account of the collision.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement both support the described impact. Damage to the vehicle is largely consistent with the reported force of the sideswipe. No prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the claimant's file.

Entry 4: Claimant was seen at an urgent care clinic the same day with knee pain and swelling, and imaging was ordered. The clinic's intake notes describe the same sequence of events the claimant gave at the scene.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant by phone to confirm the account, and the claimant described the collision the same way as in the initial report. The claimant also mentioned a past minor strain in the same knee that resolved fully with rest.

Entry 6: A neighbor who was contacted during routine inquiries believes the vehicle had visible damage some weeks before the reported collision. The neighbor's recollection is not specific about the timing or the location of the damage, so it needs follow-up.

Entry 7: Confirmed the driver lives in the policyholder's household and qualifies as a covered household member under the policy. Coverage question is resolved on that basis, and the household relationship has been documented in the file.

Entry 8: Treatment has increased sharply, with near-daily visits to the clinic and physical therapy. Pain has also been reported in the hip and lower back, which were not mentioned in the first weeks after the collision.

Entry 9: Requested the medical records from the treating providers and reviewed the billing summary. Treatment volume is many times what is typical for this type of knee injury, and the timing of the new complaints is being noted for the file.

Entry 10: Account remains consistent across all contacts, and the injury and vehicle damage both fit the reported impact. The neighbor's comment about earlier damage and the scope of the treatment remain open items, and the file is being referred for further review before any decision on the injury claim.
